author: kesudh
method: Exact shortest-path-tree warm refinement of published routes. Radix/A* trees with feasible per-sink bounds, neutral and group reroutes, preserved-route and displacement-chain repair, bounded excursions, and a multi-worker CPU search portfolio; the opt-in chain-fast modes specialize congestion pricing. Two-parent minimum-cut crossover follows the coordinated_refinement line of work by jay-tau (PR #24). Bounded conflict-based search over static vertex-disjoint multi-sink trees is an adaptation of Sharon et al. (see algorithm_references). This entry's own GPU kernels are audited prototypes and did not generate these routes.

selection: The best independently legal output per case, as reported by the official checker; ties keep the earlier route. Timed multiworker search is nondeterministic, so a repeat can return a different legal route.

algorithm_references.method: conflict splitting, adapted to static vertex-disjoint multi-sink trees
algorithm_references.citation: Sharon, Stern, Felner and Sturtevant, Conflict-based search for optimal multi-agent pathfinding

hardware: 13th Gen Intel Core i7-13700HX (16 cores / 24 threads), 31.7 GB RAM, Windows 11
runtime_scope: Per case, runtime.json reports: (1) for this entry's own routes, the wall-clock seconds of the run of this entry's router that produced the shipped file - a fixed 30 s search budget on 4 worker threads, chain-fast mode, the engine's own END_TO_END_SECONDS - except stress/case_01 (44.771 s; the budget is checked only at the top of the trial loop and a single 901-net trial can exceed it) and congested/case_01 (31.617 s: the 30.067 s run that produced the previous route plus a 1.55 s single-thread partition-crossover run); (2) for a route carried verbatim whose producing author published a runtime for that exact file, that author's own runtime, read from their runtime.json at the credited commit (14 files; each case's runtime_source names it); (3) for a carried route whose producer published none (12 files), one run of this entry's router on the instance (30 s, 4 workers, chain-fast, seed 1) warm-started from the shipped file, which returns it unchanged - that run re-produces the route but did not originate it, as each case's runtime_source states. Runs of this router were measured concurrently, so their wall-clock values are conservative.
